proposed.text: A senior architect reviews a transit terminal design and finds the accessible parking stalls are 3500 mm wide with a 1500 mm shared aisle, located at the far end of the lot. Which two non-compliances must be corrected under BP 344 2024 Revised IRR?

options.text: Stall must be 4000 mm x 5000 mm (the extra 1500 mm width forms the access aisle, not a separate strip); stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance
Stall must be 4000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance
Stall must be 4000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; vertical clearance must be 2300 mm
Stall must be 5000 mm wide with a separate 1800 mm access aisle; stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance

proposed.rationale: Correct answer: A. BP 344 specifies a single accessible parking slot of 4000 mm x 5000 mm; the additional 1500 mm width (versus an average slot) IS the access aisle that accommodates wheelchair passage — it is not a separate 1800 mm strip. Stalls must also be on the shortest accessible route to the accessible entrance, so the far-end location is a non-compliance. Source verbatim (BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, PDF p.7 lines 283-285): 'A minimum width of 4000 mm and a length of 5000 mm. The additional 1500 mm width, in comparison to the average parking slot, is intended to ensure that the adjacent pathway adequately accommodates wheelchair passage.'
proposed.explanation: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR (Appendix C, PDF p.7) defines the accessible parking slot as 4000 mm x 5000 mm, where the 1500 mm additional width relative to an average slot forms the access aisle for wheelchair deployment — options citing a separate 1800 mm aisle (B, C, D) are not in the source. A separate 1200 mm clear walkway is required between the front ends of parked cars (PDF p.7 line 286). Stalls must be nearest the accessible entrance; placing them at the far end of the lot is a location non-compliance. The 3500 mm stall width in the stem is below the 4000 mm minimum and is the dimensional non-compliance.
